## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Confirmed correctness and recovery finding |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium |
| Task Type | Focused workflow projection ordering and regression coverage |

### What Was Claimed

After the merge API succeeds, post-merge artifact, close, cleanup, or terminal work can fail before the `workflow:merged` label is projected. A durable merge can therefore remain visible as `workflow:awaiting-merge`.

### What We Found

The repository has both dispatcher-owned parent nodes and a legacy/direct finalizer. The normal merge paths record durable merge evidence and invoke the merged projection before `postReviewCompletionArtifacts`, but the invariant is not centralized across recovery paths. Direct terminal recovery waits until cleanup and terminal projection before setting the merged label. More importantly, projection reconciliation examines a completed run, then the latest node or phase; a durable merge effect with a still-running merge node is currently rendered as `workflow:awaiting-merge`. If post-merge work fails after the merge effect is durable, reconciliation can therefore regress or preserve the wrong label.

### Root Cause

Successful merge evidence and the issue-label projection are not treated as the first post-merge side effect in every execution/recovery path, and reconciliation does not prioritize durable merge evidence over an in-progress merge node. Post-merge work is allowed to run before the durable merged projection is guaranteed.

### Affected Files

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — merge, direct-finalization, terminal recovery, and projection reconciliation ordering.
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` — focused regression coverage for durable merge projection precedence and ordering.

### Evidence

- `#runParentNode` records `effectType: "merge"`, projects `workflow:merged`, then posts review completion artifacts; a later failure leaves the merge node incomplete.
- `#finalize` appends merge effect and `merge` phase completion before post-review, close, cleanup, and terminal work; its projection must remain ahead of all failure-prone post-merge operations.
- `#recoverDirectTerminal` projects `workflow:merged` only after branch/worktree cleanup and terminal event work.
- `#reconcileWorkflowProjection` maps a latest running `merge` node through `workflowStageForNodeTransition`, which returns `awaitingMerge`, without first checking merge effects or completed merge evidence.
- `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE` defines `workflow:merged` and `workflow:awaiting-merge` as distinct canonical states.

### History Findings

Issue #119 carries the review-finding fingerprint from PR #117 (`workflow-correctness-001`). The cited failure window is consistent with the current split merge/finalization/recovery implementation; no unrelated history or scope expansion is required.

### Recommendation

Project `workflow:merged` immediately after any successful or durably observed merge and before append/artifact/close/cleanup work in every merge path. Add a durable-merge-evidence predicate used by reconciliation so an incomplete post-merge node cannot overwrite the merged projection with `workflow:awaiting-merge`. Add focused tests for evidence precedence and the source-level ordering contract.

### Related Issues

- Issue `#119` (this remediation).
- Source review finding `workflow-correctness-001` from PR `#117`.

### Decomposition Assessment

Single-concern change. The fix is bounded to merge projection ordering, durable reconciliation, and regression tests; no decomposition is warranted.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Validate the cited merge/post-merge failure window against current workflow paths.
- [ ] Project `workflow:merged` before failure-prone post-merge work in normal and recovery paths.
- [ ] Prefer durable merge evidence during projection reconciliation.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage.
- [ ] Preserve the existing branch, review, merge-authority, and artifact contracts.
